summary: Black Drift duel: Abby answers a rival captain without a speech.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT HAVEN — OPEN SALVAGE GANTRY — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Rival Captain
dialogueInline.text: You don't give orders on my deck.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then get off mine.

directionInline: Open on the salvage gantry with crews ringed around a practical dispute that has already turned physical. The rival captain blocks Abby's path and says the first line. Abby answers while stepping inside his reach, strips the weapon in one ugly motion, and dumps him into the netted salvage pit. Final image: Abby keeps walking toward the waiting ships while somebody hauls him out; she never turns the victory into a speech.

summary: Abby's war deck: survival doctrine collides with Billie's appetite for spectacle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Feeders only. Cargo and escorts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: And if a farm takes a shot at me?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Shoot the gun.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You're no fun.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: That's the idea.

directionInline: At the engine-cowling map table, Abby physically removes Billie's marker from the farm settlements and drops it on the feeder route. Billie puts it back with one finger; Abby moves it again. Tess watches from the edge of the table. The conversation plays over that small contest, so the raid boundary is visible before anyone explains it.

summary: The Silent Triarch reduces a war to three brutal verbs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raid Mask
dialogueInline.text: Strike to feed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Trade Mask
dialogueInline.text: Flow sustains.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: Terror binds.

directionInline: Treat this as ritual, not ordinary conversation. Three masks sit above the captains; each gives one formal line and nothing else. Abby receives the decree standing, arms at her sides, and does not bow. The long silent reaction after the third line is the point of the scene.

summary: At Auric Bazaar, policy sounds different when spoken beside people who need heat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: North Ring has heat for two nights. Clinic's down to six antibiotic trays.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: And the Fleet wants half our docking revenue for escorts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The cheap route lost three ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Two.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The third one is six hours late.

directionInline: Halev walks the market while talking, checking a heater repair queue and a clinic manifest rather than giving a speech from a table. Wallace keeps pace with the account slate. Naomi arrives from the docks and corrects him without slowing down. The failed heater core and clinic queue make the stakes visible.

summary: Halev chooses the green corridor because every alternative is worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: You're really going to let the Fleet set the route?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: For one night, I'm going to let whoever gets the food here set the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: That's not reassuring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Didn't say it was.

directionInline: Halev stops beside a parent trying to restart a failed heater module while the clinic line advances under weak light. Wallace is still arguing from the slate. Halev looks from the family to the dark apartment ring beyond the canopy and makes the decision there, then points toward the docks.

summary: The Admiralty argues whether a humanitarian lane is mercy or an exposed throat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Open one lane and they'll use it to measure the wall.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then let them measure it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: And when the first freighter brings rifles?

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhyne
dialogueInline.text: Search it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: That simple?

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhyne
dialogueInline.text: No. Still our job.

directionInline: The route glows between the admirals on the council table. Dominion closes the projected corridor with two fingers as he speaks. Venn reopens only one narrow lane. Keating brings up a weapons-scan image; Rhyne answers while enlarging the civilian cargo numbers beside it. Nobody addresses the reader; they are arguing over the same live map.
panelPlan: Wide: Dominion above the council table; the proposed green lane glows inside the blockade.
Dominion closes the lane on the map. Venn reaches in and restores one narrow route.
Keating throws a weapons-scan image beside the route; Venn watches her, not the display.
Rhyne taps the civilian cargo totals. Dominion turns on him for the final exchange.

summary: Dominion permits the experiment without conceding the principle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: One lane. One window. You lose it, I close it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

directionInline: Dominion leaves the single green route active and kills every other proposed window. Venn studies the one remaining line, gives him a short acknowledgment, and turns for the door before he can make the concession feel generous.

summary: The Shards swear their war-moot with engines instead of words.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT HAVEN — EXTERIOR SALVAGE DECK — NIGHT
directionInline: Let the engines do the talking. Shard ships ring Black Drift; captains climb into mismatched hulls, deck crews pull away umbilicals, and one engine after another lights until the haven becomes a rough constellation. Abby watches the departures from the gantry. Tess catches her eye from Gravefire before sealing her hatch. No voice-over.

summary: The feint begins: Billie treats Abby's restraint as an insult and enters wanting destruction rather than leverage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Third freighter's riding low. That's ours.

directionInline: From Ashfang's cockpit, the convoy is already visible through the feeder truss. Billie ignores the best-defended lead ship and points at the third freighter sagging below formation. Her crew shifts targeting to it. The ordered Shard skiffs hold Abby's assigned spacing while Ashfang edges out of line.
panelPlan: Wide establishing panel: the tan-green civilian convoy threads a damaged feeder truss; pale-gray Shard skiffs hold an ordered attack line beyond it.
Inside Ashfang's cramped industrial-black cockpit, red targeting light catches Billie's loose red hair as she studies the convoy.
Billie's gloved finger passes over the protected lead ship and settles on the third freighter, visibly low in formation with a stressed engine plume.
The crew shifts the firing solution to the third ship as Billie claims it.
Final exterior: the other skiffs keep Abby's disciplined spacing while Ashfang noses out of line, making Billie's breach physically legible.

summary: Venn refuses the bait and chooses civilian protection while her officers expect retaliation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Three skiffs. Feeder spine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Don't chase them. Stay with the freighters.

directionInline: On Thunderbreak, attack solutions bloom automatically around the incoming skiffs. Junior officers expect the obvious pursuit. Venn cancels those vectors and drags Thunderbreak's path alongside the freighters instead. The ship becomes a moving wall because of what she does on the board.
panelPlan: Bright Fleet bridge: red pursuit solutions bloom over the luminous blue tactical table while the civilian convoy holds at its center.
A junior officer reports the skiffs and looks to Venn for the expected attack order.
Close on Venn's steady hand cancelling the pursuit vectors one by one.
Venn drags Thunderbreak's blue course alongside the tan-green freighter icons and gives the protective order.
Wide exterior payoff: the immense navy-white Thunderbreak settles beside the smaller patched freighters as a moving wall while the skiffs race away.

summary: Tessa quietly saves lives while everyone else is looking for a fight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Cut your beacon. Drift with me.

directionInline: A medpod freighter tumbles out of cover. Gravefire goes dark, catches it with micro-tethers, and pulls it into debris shadow. Tess speaks directly to the terrified freighter pilot while watching Ashfang's firing cone sweep past them. Her own crew realizes what she is doing but does not comment.
panelPlan: A small tan-green medpod freighter tumbles from the feeder structure, white medical pods visible through a ruptured cargo frame.
Tessa, silver curls lit by muted red instruments, kills Gravefire's bright systems and launches two micro-tethers.
The tethers bite; Gravefire rolls with the freighter instead of fighting its spin.
Tessa tells the terrified pilot to cut the beacon while Ashfang's red firing cone sweeps across their darkened cockpit.
Wide silent panel: Gravefire and the freighter settle into a debris shadow. Tessa's crew understands the unauthorized rescue and keeps working.

summary: Billie breaks the plan because destruction is the point for her.
directionInline: Ashfang breaks Abby's assigned vector and strafes the storage spine. Heater cells and thermal blankets burst into bright sheets of burning debris while dark civilian habitat rings sit beyond them. Hold on Billie's face only after the shot: she expected spectacle; the image outside is uglier and more wasteful than the cheer she wanted. No line tells the reader what to feel.
panelPlan: Ashfang shears away from the ordered skiff line, its bright-red drive flare cutting across Abby's plotted vector.
Billie rolls the marauder onto the exposed storage spine and fires before her crew can settle the aim.
A dominant impact panel: heater cells, sealed food tins, and bundled thermal blankets erupt into a brilliant debris sheet—not an abstract explosion.
Beyond the burning supplies, several civilian habitat rings remain dark; tiny windows and maintenance lamps establish who needed the cargo.
Close on Billie's face after the shot. Reflected fire replaces the grin she expected to wear; no dialogue explains the reaction.

summary: Thunderbreak physically blocks Billie's firing lane instead of escalating the battle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang's lining up on the clinic ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Put us between them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: That's inside her range.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I know.

directionInline: The clinic freighter fills the center of the tactical display with Ashfang's firing cone closing over it. Venn orders Thunderbreak across the cone. Exterior beat: the heavy cruiser shoulders a drifting structural beam aside and takes the exposed position itself. Sparks rake the armor when Ashfang fires past.
panelPlan: Tactical display: Ashfang's red cone closes over a visibly marked clinic freighter; Thunderbreak is outside the firing lane.
The tactical officer names the threat. Venn studies the civilian ship for one beat, then orders Thunderbreak between them.
The officer turns, understanding the range problem; Venn's quiet 'I know' ends the debate.
Large exterior panel: Thunderbreak shoulders a broken feeder beam aside and crosses into Ashfang's line, dwarfing the clinic ship without obscuring it.
Sparks rake Thunderbreak's exposed armor as fire passes close. Through the gap behind it, the clinic freighter continues moving.

summary: Naomi turns a frightened escort line into something that can hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Blue Two, you're drifting. Get back on me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Clinic pods stay inside the line. Come on—there you go.

directionInline: Naomi's escort line wobbles under pressure. One pilot slides too far out; she talks that ship back into place while her own hands shake on the controls. The medpods settle inside the protective geometry. Her fear is visible, but the dialogue is only about the immediate flying problem.
panelPlan: Inside Naomi's patched tan-green cockpit, the escort formation jitters across a scratched practical display; Blue Two drifts out of the protective arc.
Naomi orders Blue Two back while correcting her own ship with both hands. Her brow scar and clenched jaw match the released likeness.
Close on one trembling hand working the thruster controls; she never comments on the fear.
Exterior: Blue Two slides back beside Naomi's smaller escort as exposed clinic pods pass between them.
The line finally closes around the medpods. Naomi gives the gentler second instruction—'there you go'—without taking her eyes off the threat.

summary: Billie and Tessa leave the same raid with opposite lessons.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You tucked a freighter in my blind side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You had plenty to look at.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Next time I won't miss.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Then look first.

directionInline: Ashfang and Gravefire cross on opposite withdrawal vectors. Billie finally spots the rescued freighter tucked into Gravefire's debris shadow. The two captains see each other through magnified canopy feeds for the exchange; neither ship slows down.
panelPlan: Wide: Ashfang and Gravefire cross nose-to-tail on opposite withdrawal vectors amid spinning feeder debris.
Billie catches the medpod freighter tucked tight inside Gravefire's debris shadow and realizes what Tessa did.
Split cockpit panel: Billie, vivid red hair and hot anger; Tessa, silver curls and exhausted calm. Their magnified canopy feeds lock eyelines.
Billie threatens not to miss next time while Ashfang continues past instead of turning to attack.
Tessa answers 'Then look first.' Final exterior separates the two ships, with the rescued freighter still protected behind Gravefire.

summary: Jex sells Halev what institutions cannot quite provide: a compromise that can function now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I don't think we can get by with any less than eight ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: That's six more than you have now. I can give you four additional.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I said I need six from you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Maybe you need another smuggler.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Do you know any other smugglers?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Okay. Five.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Fine. Five. I'm either getting weak or lazy. Dammit. Five.

directionInline: Halev's office overlooks the docks. Two battered supply ships sit outside while the manifest on the desk shows the eight hulls Halev says he needs. Jex keeps doing the arithmetic on the physical slate as if the shortage were Halev's problem. Naomi stays near the window and says nothing. After Jex asks whether Halev knows another smuggler, Halev lets the silence sit before offering five. Jex's final complaint lands while he physically adds the fifth ship to the manifest.
panelPlan: Wide office/docks: two available supply ships are visible beyond Halev and Jex; the manifest shows a required total of eight.
Jex taps the two existing ships on the slate and adds four more while answering.
Halev does not move when he repeats that he needs six from Jex.
Jex leans back from the slate and asks whether Halev knows another smuggler. Naomi watches from the window.
Silence on Halev. Then: 'Okay. Five.'
Jex irritably adds the fifth ship to the manifest and complains that he is getting weak or lazy.

summary: Naomi and Jex establish their relationship while Halev accepts a temporary authority he does not trust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: No inspections?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: You want them on time?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Rapid scans. No holds unless somebody finds a weapon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: And disputes?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: You. For now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: He's going to make that his title.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Already did.

directionInline: The five-ship deal is now written on a slate between them. Naomi takes the slate and reads the inspection clause aloud. Halev edits the terms with a stylus while Jex watches for the one provision that gives him leverage. When Halev gives him temporary arbitration authority, Jex immediately stamps his own mark beside it. Naomi sees what he has done before Halev does.
panelPlan: Continue at the same desk: the five-ship agreement fills the physical slate; the battered ships remain visible through the office window.
Naomi takes the slate and challenges the missing inspection language while Jex watches her over it.
Halev writes rapid scans and no holds into the agreement as working dock crews move below.
Jex asks about disputes and already has his personal stamp ready under one hand.
Halev grants temporary authority. Jex stamps his mark beside the clause before Halev has lifted the stylus.
Naomi notices first and warns Halev; Jex's 'Already did' lands on the newly stamped title.

summary: The first corridor tests whether armed rivals can all choose not to fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Blue Three, ease left. That's it. Hold there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak is outside your lane. Weapons cold.

directionInline: The first five freighters enter the green markers with heater cores, medpods, batteries and food visible through cargo apertures. Naomi is busy correcting one escort's spacing; Venn's confirmation comes over comms while Thunderbreak holds just outside the lane. Tess appears at the far edge without announcing herself. The tension comes from armed ships watching one another and choosing not to fire.
panelPlan: Tall establishing panel: five patched tan-green freighters enter a narrow chain of green markers through fractured rift debris; heater cores, medpods, batteries, and food are materially visible.
Naomi corrects Blue Three from her cramped escort cockpit while keeping the civilian hulls centered.
Thunderbreak holds outside the marked lane, weapons ports visibly dark. Venn confirms weapons cold from the luminous Fleet bridge.
At the opposite edge, Gravefire resolves from shadow with Tessa watching, equally armed and equally still.
Wide silent panel across all three forces: targeting brackets hover but do not lock. The convoy advances because everyone chooses not to fire.

summary: Billie tests the corridor and discovers Abby can still stop her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You're really stopping me for this?

directionInline: Ashfang creeps toward the convoy. In a shadowed skiff ahead, Abby raises one unmistakable hand command: stop. Billie sees it reflected on her canopy, looks from Abby to the vulnerable freighter, and reluctantly throttles down. Abby never answers.
panelPlan: Ashfang emerges from rift shadow behind the convoy, closing on the weakest freighter with weapons still dark.
Inside Ashfang, Billie sees the target and advances the throttle despite the green corridor markers.
A smaller pale-gray skiff slides across her approach. Through its canopy, Abby raises one flat hand: stop.
The raised hand reflects across Billie's canopy beside the vulnerable freighter; Billie asks whether Abby is really stopping her for this.
Close on Abby's unanswering, tired face. Final insert: Billie's hand pulls the throttle back.

summary: Jex runs the corridor from a back room and prepares to survive either outcome.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: If this works, it was my corridor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: If it doesn't, you've never met me.

directionInline: Jex runs the crossing from a cramped back room where runners are constantly entering and leaving with beacon codes, bribe lists and arbitration slates. He signs one authorization while shoving a second toward a waiting runner. The two lines are tossed to different people without stopping the work.
panelPlan: Establish the Veil Market back room as a working route exchange: patched walls, handwritten beacon codes, bribe lists, cargo seals, and too many waiting runners.
Jex signs one authorization while a runner reports the corridor still open; he never stops sorting the next slate.
He hands the signed code to one runner—'If this works, it was my corridor.'
Without looking up, he shoves a different ledger toward another runner—'If it doesn't, you've never met me.'
Final overhead panel: runners leave in opposite directions while Jex remains at the crowded center of the information flow.

summary: The corridor's first anomaly appears and everyone has to resist shooting at a ghost.
settingText: GREEN CORRIDOR — MARKERS ONE AND TWO

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Mark One clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Mark Two— what the hell is that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Nobody fire. Just hold.

directionInline: At Mark Two, a ghost freighter slides into existence directly beside the real one. Across multiple cockpits, fingers move toward triggers. Naomi sees the duplicate at the same moment as everyone else and has to catch herself mid-call. The final panel holds both freighters side by side while nobody fires.
panelPlan: Naomi watches the lead freighter clear Mark One and calls it.
At Mark Two, a second impossible freighter begins to resolve beside the real one; Naomi stops mid-call.
Quick reactions across opposing cockpits: hands near triggers, eyes on targeting displays.
Naomi, staring at the duplicate: nobody fires. Final wide holds the real and ghost freighters together.

summary: Venn registers a tiny victory in operational language while a junior officer sees what it cost her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Log the crossing. Keep the lane open.

directionInline: The last cargo icon crosses the boundary. The junior officer exhales, then notices Venn briefly steadying two fingers against the console edge. She catches the look, removes her hand, and immediately turns back to the route. Her line is a work order because that is how she allows herself relief.
panelPlan: On Thunderbreak's luminous route display, the last tan-green cargo icon crosses the boundary while all weapon indicators remain cold.
The junior officer reports the clearance and finally exhales.
Close on Venn's hand: two fingers steady against the polished console edge, the only visible release after sustained control.
The officer notices. Venn catches the look and removes her hand before either acknowledges it.
Venn turns back to the open route and disguises victory as maintenance: 'Log the crossing. Keep the lane open.'

summary: Halev sees cargo icons as the concrete lives they will change.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Heaters to North Ring. Antibiotics to the clinic. Batteries stay here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Keep unloading.

directionInline: Halev is already on the dock when the freighters arrive. Crates come down around him faster than clerks can tag them. He redirects three loads by pointing them toward waiting carts, then looks up only long enough to see apartment windows beginning to light in the distance.
panelPlan: Auric dock arrival: battered freighters unload into a crowded tan-green working port; clerks, handcarts, and repair crews are already overwhelmed.
Halev reads actual crate markings—heater cores, antibiotics, battery stacks—not abstract cargo icons.
He points each load toward a different waiting cart while giving the three terse destinations.
Workers split the cargo streams immediately; a clinic orderly takes the antibiotics as North Ring crews haul heater units away.
Halev looks past the moving crates to distant apartment windows beginning to light, then returns to the dock: 'Keep unloading.'

summary: Abby admits why she let the convoy pass; Tessa offers a different future without demanding an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You stopped Billie.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I stopped her wasting our next clinic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Sure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Didn't say anything.

directionInline: Abby stands at the casualty board updating a clinic inventory beside the green-route display. Tess comes in behind her and notices what Abby is doing before she speaks. Abby never turns around during the exchange. Tess's 'Sure' is almost neutral; Abby hears the implication anyway. Tess leaves her with the board rather than pressing for a confession.
panelPlan: Abby alone at the casualty board, moving clinic stock numbers beside the green route.
Tess enters behind her and notices the inventory before saying Abby stopped Billie.
Abby keeps writing while giving the practical excuse.
Tess says 'Sure.' Abby finally looks back: 'Don't.'
Tess raises both hands slightly—'Didn't say anything.'—and leaves. Abby returns to the clinic numbers.

summary: Naomi and Venn acknowledge each other's contribution with restrained professional warmth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Verge convoy to Thunderbreak. Thanks for the shadow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: You brought them through, Captain.

directionInline: The freighters peel toward Auric docks. Cut between Naomi's patched Verge cockpit and Venn's luminous Fleet bridge for the restrained acknowledgment carried forward from the released Issue 1 QC. Neither woman makes it larger than it is; both return to work immediately after.
panelPlan: Naomi watches the last freighter peel toward the docks and opens the channel to Thunderbreak.
Close on Naomi, braid and brow scar matching released canon: 'Thanks for the shadow.'
Venn receives the gratitude without smiling for an audience and gives the achievement back to Naomi.
Wide closing panel: the patched Verge convoy heads for Auric while Thunderbreak remains outside the lane; both women have already returned to their controls.

summary: Billie's restraint holds only because Abby has temporarily imposed it; her threat becomes personal and tactical.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Next time, I choose the mark.

directionInline: Ashfang idles nose-to-nose with Abby's smaller skiff after the convoy is gone. Billie is still hot from being stopped; Abby looks tired rather than triumphant. The threat is private and close-range, not a declaration to the fleet. Abby does not answer; the power lies in the fact that Billie stopped.
panelPlan: After the convoy clears, Ashfang turns and settles nose-to-nose with Abby's smaller skiff against the empty green markers.
Inside Ashfang, Billie leans toward the canopy, red hair bright against the dark cockpit, anger replacing the earlier thrill.
Inside the opposing skiff, Abby remains seated and still, long braids and pale-gray command coat matching released canon; she looks exhausted, not victorious.
Billie makes the threat—'Next time, I choose the mark.'—as the two ships hold dangerous proximity.
Abby gives no reply. Ashfang finally peels away first.

summary: Jex recognizes that a temporary compromise has made him structurally necessary and intends to own that dependency.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Now they need the road. Tomorrow they need me.

directionInline: Jex's office door opens onto a new line of captains, merchants and petitioners holding corridor requests. He looks at the pile already on his desk, then at the longer line outside. He states the dependency he has recognized without a toast or victory pose, sits down, and pulls the first slate toward him.
panelPlan: Jex's office door opens from darkness onto a corridor now crowded with captains, merchants, clinic agents, and freight petitioners holding route slates.
Jex looks from the unfinished pile on his desk to the much longer line outside; the successful corridor has created visible administrative demand.
Close on his older, creased face as he understands the leverage: 'Now they need the road.'
He sits, draws the first slate toward him, and completes the thought: 'Tomorrow they need me.'
Final issue image: the first petitioner steps in while the line continues beyond the doorway; the road is open, but access already has a broker.
